originality.rationale: Primary Lambert reflection and eccentric shifts are known, so novelty is restricted to the mathematically exact fold/unique peak dominance phase diagram for a fixed physically motivated alignment. residual_risks: The qualitative existence of eccentricity-shifted/multiple peaks is established in Dyudina et al.; only the exact classified transition is asserted as new.
A general extremum theorem for Lambertian phase curves or convex scattering functions could imply the result without matching its numerical constants.
The exact edge-on periastron/new-phase geometry is a special parameter slice; literature indexed under phase curves could conceal a stronger theorem.

value.rationale: Global phase curves can exhibit competing maxima in eccentric reflected-light models. The mathematical question of whether a newly formed secondary peak becomes dominant is well motivated and not answered by merely plotting a shifted maximum. The sharp double threshold, one-crossing theorem, three-maxima interval and universal square-root onset constitute a complete useful boundary classification for the ideal Lambert reference case; physical visibility limitations are disclosed.
